description:
Staff identity with roles (box office / admin / finance), the event & inventory builder UI, order management console (lookup, refund, exchange, resend, holds).

**Conditions of Success:**
- Role matrix enforced server-side; box-office staff cannot touch settlement
- Organizer builds a sellable event end-to-end in the UI without API calls
- Console handles the full order lifecycle staff-side

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Scope anchor (owner decision 2026-07-14):** this epic owns the organizer-facing **catalog builder UI** — the screens to author events, series, seasons, festivals and the typed dated-slot kinds (performance / festival_day / operating_day) plus their publish/archive lifecycle — over the catalog API built in **TKT-2** (children TKT-49…TKT-53). TKT-2 deliberately ships API + storefront only ("creation via API only", per the TKT-26 precedent); the builder UI and the staff identity/RBAC it sits behind are consolidated here so the organizer never touches curl. Decomposing TKT-22 must therefore depend on the relevant TKT-2 catalog endpoints being stable, and cover series/season/festival/slot authoring — not just the M1 single-GA-event shape.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Decomposed into five vertical slices, chained by dependency:

| Child | Slice | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| TKT-190 | US-B1: Staff sign-in — a session gates the back office | — |
| TKT-191 | US-B2: The role matrix — box office cannot touch settlement | TKT-190 |
| TKT-192 | US-B3: Event builder — publish a sellable event without curl | TKT-191 |
| TKT-193 | US-B4: Order console — find an order, read its lifecycle | TKT-191 |
| TKT-194 | US-B5: Order console actions — refund and resend | TKT-193 |

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | ✅ | `make check`, contract tests, **browser-submit** for every UI story, ADR-004 tier per read |
| Vertical slices | ✅ | Each child crosses schema→backend→UI→tests and is demoable alone |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | US-B1 *is* the prefactor: the principal every later child gates on |
| Ordered by dependency | ✅ | No forward dependency; B3 and B4 are siblings off B2 and may run in either order |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Every COS names an observable outcome; no "works correctly" |
| Links + cycle check | ✅ | Chain is a tree rooted at B1 — walked transitively, no cycle |
| Context-mémo per child | ✅ | `governingAdrs` resolved against `docs/adr/` at HEAD; every cited file verified present |
| No unvalidated assumption | ⚠️ | See concern 1 |

**Concerns:**
1. **TKT-190 — where staff identity lives is undecided.** ADR-002 cuts the system at five services plus a gateway, and the gateway owns no database today. The two candidates (a gateway-owned staff store enforcing at the edge, vs. a sixth `identity` service) are a real architecture decision, not a coding detail. It is carried as `approach: deferred` with an ADR as an explicit US-B1 deliverable, rather than pre-decided here.
2. **TKT-190 — a session cookie arrives while `checkOrigin` is disabled.** `web/backoffice/astro.config.mjs` sets `security.checkOrigin:false`, justified in TKT-105 by "the gateway is the trust boundary … no auth yet". US-B1 removes that premise, so its CSRF posture must be stated and enforced (`SameSite`), not inherited.
3. **TKT-194 — the console will surface known-open gaps.** A failed compensation refund has no automated path forward (TKT-144) and no operator unpark path (TKT-146); refunded tickets still admit at an OFFLINE gate (TKT-162). US-B5 must not render success or finality over any of those. Scoped by COS, not fixed here.
4. **No browser/e2e harness exists in-repo.** The browser-submit gate is real (TKT-105) but manual, and this epic is four UI stories. Each story carries the cost; expect the verification evidence to say precisely how the submit was driven.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable. The decomposition is sound and dependency-clean; the named risks are design decisions deliberately routed to the plan gate (1, 2) and pre-existing platform gaps the children are scoped to respect rather than paper over (3, 4).

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Gate 1 — waived by the repo owner (run of 2026-08-03).**

The owner is running TKT-22 and its children **fully autonomously, Ready → Done, gateless**, as a
deliberate process experiment. All four human gates are waived for this run:

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human moves Backlog → Ready | **granted up front** by the owner for TKT-22 and every child |
| 2 — plan approval | human moves Planning → Building | agent resolves open decisions itself: take the plan-critique's recommendation; absent one, take the **most reversible** option. Every self-made decision is recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | human reviews the PR and squash-merges | agent squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules). The **review-guide is still posted first** — it is the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates COS and moves to Done | agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on the **merged** code, posts the validation note, closes with the full `kind=metrics` comment. |

**Unchanged and non-negotiable for this run:** `config.models` routing with no substitutions
(plan → `gpt-5.6-sol`, planReview → main-agent, implement → main-agent, aiReview → `gpt-5.6-sol`),
cross-model review for both plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green
before every push **and after every merge**, every marker comment posted at its stage, and no AI
attribution anywhere in commits or PRs.

**The agent stops and reports instead of proceeding if:** the gate or CI fails twice on the same
cause with no clear fix; the work would touch auth, money paths, data migrations or CI/deploy
config in a way the ticket and plan did not anticipate; a blocking review finding survives the
churn cap; a configured model is unreachable after the escalation ladder; or a destructive,
hard-to-reverse action has no unambiguously right choice.

Recorded here so the board history shows this ticket ran gateless.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Epic closeout — TKT-22: Back office & staff RBAC

**Six stories, all Done, run gateless end to end as a process experiment.**

| Story | | Diff | Findings | Passes | Gate runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TKT-190 | US-B1 staff sign-in | ~3,000 | 9 | 4 | 6 |
| TKT-191 | US-B2a catalog authenticates the deputy | ~1,100 | 4 | 2 | 4 |
| TKT-197 | US-B2b the role matrix | ~1,300 | 5 | 2 | 3 |
| TKT-192 | US-B3 event builder | ~900 | 24 | 4 | 9 |
| TKT-193 | US-B4 order console | ~960 | 9 | 4 | 9 |
| TKT-194 | US-B5 refund | ~2,670 | 8 | 4 | 7 |
| | **total** | **~9,900** | **59** | **20** | **38** |

**Ready → Done, all six: ~20 hours. human-wait: ~0.** Two human inputs after the waiver — a scope
decision on TKT-193 and a role decision on TKT-194 — both taken in under a minute and both changing
what shipped.

---

### The number this experiment produced

**41 of 59 findings — nearly 70% — were defects in code written to fix an earlier finding.**

Not in the implementations. In the *fixes*. Every ticket showed it, and the two hardest hit the
absolute churn cap of 4 with `[high]` findings still landing at the cap.

**This is the experiment's main result.** A single adversarial review pass over an AI-written diff
would have caught roughly a third of what was actually wrong. The rest only surfaced because each
round reviewed the previous round's repair — and the repairs were written fast, under momentum,
against one example, by an author who had just been told they were wrong and was motivated to close.

### The second result: what mutation checks caught that four reviewers did not

**~70 mutation checks across the epic.** Three found defects no review pass found:

- a fixture uuid with no hex letters, making a case-insensitivity test unable to fail (TKT-193);
- `Number('0x10') === 16` and `Number('1e1') === 10`, both inside a 1..50 bound, leaving a
  digits-only regex load-bearing and untested (TKT-194);
- a mutation check run under a `-run` filter that excluded the test that would catch it — **a
  meta-instance of the same failure** (TKT-194).

The rule that a test written *while fixing a finding* gets the same mutation check as a planned one
landed in `SKILL.md` mid-epic (`143f3a6e`), after four such tests had already shipped unable to fail.
TKT-193 was the first ticket run under it and immediately found one.

### Third: two of six stories rested on data that did not exist

TKT-193 asked for buyer contact, line items and money totals — `OrderState` is `{order_id, status}`
with `additionalProperties: false`. TKT-194 asked for a resend — no endpoint exists in any service.
Both cleared Gate 1 with `approach: deferred`; both were caught at claim time, costing a rescope each.
`shaping.md` now refuses `deferred` on auth/money/migration/CI tickets. The unapplied half of that
lesson: **a COS that names data should name the read that supplies it.**

### What the back office can actually do now

Staff sign in against bcrypt-hashed credentials with a role; a fail-closed route matrix decides what
each role reaches, and a page with no rule fails the build. An admin builds an event end to end —
event, dated slot, price, publish — and the result is reservable through the storefront. Box office
looks up an order, reads each ticket's lifecycle history, and refunds. Catalog and commerce each
authenticate the back office as a **deputy** through their own narrowly-scoped credential; neither
is the shared internal token, and the gateway's `/internal/` deny has no exceptions.

### What it deliberately cannot

No resend (**TKT-203**). No buyer contact, line items or money totals (**TKT-201**). No refund
approval, cap, or review surface — **unowned, and named in ADR-042 rather than implied**. No login
rate limiting (**TKT-195**). Cross-tenant publish is open (**TKT-199**), catalog creates take no
idempotency key (**TKT-200**), and the gateway logs `guest_order_ref` against ADR-012 (**TKT-202**).

### Filed during the run

TKT-195, TKT-196, TKT-198, TKT-199, TKT-200, TKT-201, TKT-202, TKT-203 — eight tickets, none of them
scope creep absorbed into a story.

### The decisions

**ADR-042**, created by TKT-190 and amended three times — by TKT-191 (catalog authenticates the
deputy), TKT-197 (the deputy's rule is the role matrix) and TKT-194 (the back office holds a second
credential, and it moves money). Each amendment supersedes a claim **in place while keeping the
argument that produced it**, which is what made the last one narrow: the reason not to hold
`INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` is exactly the reason the commerce credential opens one operation.

### For whoever runs the next epic this way

1. **Budget for the fix diff, not the implementation.** It is where two thirds of the defects were.
2. **The churn cap is the sharpest open question.** Four passes was not enough on the two hardest
   tickets. A money or auth path may deserve more, or a rule that a `[high]` at the cap blocks.
3. **Mutation-check the thing the assertion names**, not the code near it — and check the mutation
   ran the test you meant.
4. **Gateless worked, and the two human decisions mattered.** Both changed what shipped, and neither
   took a minute. The experiment's honest reading is not "humans are unnecessary" but "humans were
   needed twice in twenty hours, at moments an agent could identify and name."
